# Gauntlet — Iteration 02

**Subject:** Tiger I Ausf. H, Henschel, late February 1943 — complete vehicle, no crew stations
**Suite:** 243 tests passing across 20 files, `GAUNTLET_EXIT=0`, 76,752 triangles
**Views:** `docs/gauntlet/renders/` — five orthographic, four three-quarter, five silhouettes, nine details, two interiors
**Numerical QA:** `docs/gauntlet/numerical-qa.md`, generated by the test suite, 19 rows, all inside tolerance

---

## Verdict

# REJECT

At iteration 01 four of the six critics had nothing in front of them. All six
now do, and the model has gone from a hull to a recognisable Tiger: interleaved
running gear, 192 track links on a solved belt, the turret with a working drum
cupola, the 8.8 cm KwK 36, and an interior you can climb into through a hatch
that opens.

It is rejected on Critic 6 and Critic 1. The crew stations do not exist —
there are no seats, no controls, no instruments, no gun breech and no ammunition
— so the interior is a set of compartments rather than a place anyone worked.
Several exterior items that both supplied photographs show are also absent.

Nothing here is a structural fault. That is a change from iteration 01, where
two were.

---

## What the numbers say now

Nineteen measured rows, every one inside tolerance. Four of them are worth
pulling out because nothing was tuned to make them land:

| Check | Reference | Model | Why it is not circular |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hull length, nose to rear plate | 6,316 mm | **6,317** | Falls out of four plate angles and three transition heights |
| Overall length, gun forward | 8,450 mm | **8,246** | Trunnion position, L/56 barrel and muzzle brake, all specified separately |
| Height to cupola top | 3,000 mm | **2,940** | Ring plane + turret height + two roof plates + drum, five independent estimates |
| Belt path vs track length | 12,480 mm | **12,510** | Sprocket and idler positions against 96 links at 130 mm pitch |

The last one earned its keep: it was 184 mm out, and chasing that discrepancy is
what found both pulley centres sitting too high.

---

## Critic 1 — Historical accuracy · REJECT

**What holds.** Every configuration decision for late February 1943 is
enforced by `src/spec/variants.ts` and now visible in the geometry: the drum
cupola, the 25 mm turret roof, TWO mantlet sight apertures for the binocular
TZF 9b, Feifel pre-cleaners, the Rommelkiste and NbK 39 dischargers together
(a five-month overlap), 18-bolt road wheel rims, no return rollers, and the
January 1943 triangular track guard ends.

| # | Finding | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| 1.3 | Interlocking teeth still absent from every plate joint. Deferred to the detail pass under R2, and still open. | Major |
| 1.5 | **239 of 359 spec values are `estimated`** — two thirds. Most are shape and position rather than principal dimensions, but the proportion is the honest headline of this report. | Major |
| 1.6 | No tow cables, no jack, no track tools, no fire extinguisher, no aerial. Both supplied photographs show the first of those. | Major |
| 1.7 | No markings: no turret numbers, no Balkenkreuz. `REF-photo-2` carries "231" and a cross; `REF-photo-3` carries "12". | Minor |

**REJECT** on 1.5 and 1.6.

## Critic 2 — Hull geometry · PASS

Every plate is a closed solid; manifold audits, signed volume, ray-march
thickness and symmetry all pass. All hull rows in the numerical QA are inside
tolerance, and the frontal arrangement is four distinct planes with a 146°
included angle at the step where a wedge would read 180°.

Findings 2.2 through 2.8 from iteration 01 are corrected. What remains:

| # | Finding | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| 2.5 | The engine deck hatch is still an aperture with no lid. | Minor |
| 2.9 | No rear towing pintle; the rear plate is bare where the drawing shows fittings. | Minor |

**PASS.** Nothing structural is outstanding.

## Critic 3 — Turret and gun · REJECT

The turret is a horseshoe of 80 mm plate with a 100 mm front plate and a 25 mm
roof, and the drum cupola's **five vision slits are genuine apertures** — a ray
sweep out of the drum reads open across ±7°, solid from 9° to 63°, open again at
66°, five times round. That is requirement R1 and it holds.

| # | Finding | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| 3.1 | No hatch lids on the cupola or the loader's hatch. Both are open holes. | Major |
| 3.2 | No escape hatch and no pistol port. Both are in the curved rear wall, which the current shell primitive cannot cut through — the wall is one extruded plate. | Major |
| 3.3 | No gun breech, no recoil guard, no elevation gear, no coaxial MG. The turret interior is empty. | Major |
| 3.4 | The gun does not elevate. The trunnion frame exists and takes an angle; nothing drives it. | Major |
| 3.5 | `UNCERTAINTY #3` (elevation limits) and `#4` (mantlet thickness) remain open. | Minor |

**REJECT** on 3.1 through 3.4.

## Critic 4 — Running gear · REJECT

48 road wheels in three interleaved rows, eight swing arms and torsion bars a
side, sprockets, idlers, and 192 individual track links on a belt path that is
the convex hull of the pulleys — which is what a taut belt physically is, and
which cannot produce a path that cuts through a wheel.

| # | Finding | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| 4.4 | No shock absorbers on stations 1 and 8, no sprocket or idler spokes, and the idler is fixed where the spec puts it rather than positioned by its draw bolts. | Major |
| 4.5 | `UNCERTAINTY #9` open: the wheel rows span 465 mm of a 725 mm track, and the drawing's front elevation cannot settle the true spread because the track hides the wheels in that view. | Major |
| 4.7 | The suspension does not deflect. `axleCentre` takes a deflection angle and the arm droop is derived correctly; nothing drives it, so the tank does not settle or roll. | Major |

**REJECT** on 4.4 and 4.7.

## Critic 5 — Visual quality · PASS

Findings 5.1 through 5.3 are corrected. The speckle had two separate causes —
fine noise keeping full contrast below a pixel, and every plate rim being given
an edge distance of zero regardless of how deep the plate was extruded — and
both are fixed at the source rather than tuned away.

| # | Finding | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| 5.4 | Edge treatment is still uneven. Deferred under **R3**, correctly not started. | Deferred |
| 5.5 | The interior is lit only by what comes through the hatches and vision ports. Historically true and visually very dark; a Tiger had interior lamps. | Minor |

**PASS**, with R3 outstanding by agreement.

## Critic 6 — Reference match · REJECT

| Feature | Reference | Model | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| Overall silhouette | Complete vehicle | Complete vehicle | **Now comparable** |
| Frontal plate arrangement | Nose / short glacis / driver's plate | Four distinct planes, 146° at the step | ok |
| Hull MG side | Viewer's left, head-on | Viewer's left | ok |
| Cupola side | Port, drawn plainly in the plan view | Port | ok |
| Engine deck grilles | Four, two a side fore and aft of an access panel | Four | ok |
| Feifel trunking | Converging on a drum on the centreline | Converging on a drum | ok |
| Track guards | Projecting ahead of the nose, triangular ends | 3,468 mm against 3,480 measured | ok |
| Tow cables on the hull side | Present in both photographs | **Absent** | Major |
| Turret markings | "231" and a Balkenkreuz | **Absent** | Minor |
| Crew stations | Cutaway shows seats, controls, breech, ammunition | **Absent** | Critical |

**REJECT** on the last row. The cutaway is the reference this model is furthest
from, and it is the one that shows what a Tiger is like to be inside.

---

## Required corrections before the next gauntlet

1. Crew stations: seats, driver's controls and instruments, radio racks (6.1).
2. Gun breech, recoil guard and coaxial mount; make the gun elevate (3.3, 3.4).
3. Cupola and loader's hatch lids, on their real mechanisms (3.1).
4. Suspension deflection, so the vehicle settles on its torsion bars (4.7).
5. Escape hatch and pistol port, which needs the turret shell rebuilt as
   segments the way the cupola already is (3.2).
6. Tow cables, tools and stowage (1.6).
7. Shock absorbers, sprocket and idler spokes, idler tensioning (4.4).
8. Interlocking teeth, and the R3 edge pass, in the Stage 9 detail pass.

## What this iteration says about the method

Every fault found this round was found by something mechanical, and three of
them by tests that were not looking for them:

- The **R1 vision tests** failed because a gearbox was in the radio operator's
  line of fire. They exist to check that ports are real openings; they caught a
  layout error two subsystems away.
- The **numerical QA** caught the road wheels 200 mm underground, then the whole
  track hanging through the ground plane, then the wheels resting on the ground
  rather than on the track. Three separate faults, one row.
- The **track's own length** — a sourced 96 links at 130 mm pitch — caught both
  pulley centres 200 mm too high.

Against that, the two faults that most needed catching in iteration 01 were
found by a person looking at a picture. The lesson has not changed since:
mechanical checks catch what they were pointed at and what happens to cross
their path, and neither of those is the same as catching what is wrong.
